new_entities.name: Subsymptom-threshold aerobic exercise after concussion
new_entities.description: Aerobic exercise prescribed below the symptom-provocation threshold during concussion recovery.

new_entities.name: Recovery time
new_entities.description: The duration required to recover or become medically cleared.

edges.effect_quant: In the key adolescent concussion trial, subthreshold aerobic exercise shortened median recovery from 17 to 13 days compared with placebo-like stretching, and a later randomized study also found faster asymptomatic status and medical clearance with structured early aerobic exercise.
edges.population: adolescents and young adults recovering from sport-related concussion, including persistent-symptom cohorts
edges.mechanism: Subsymptom aerobic exercise may normalize autonomic and cerebrovascular regulation, reduce deconditioning, and provide a controlled graded exposure to exertion without repeatedly triggering symptom flares. The main point is not high intensity, but carefully staying below the threshold that worsens symptoms.
edges.summary: The best current evidence supports early, individualized subsymptom aerobic exercise as a way to shorten concussion recovery time. Multiple randomized trials point in the same direction, so this edge is one of the cleaner active-rehabilitation signals in the concussion literature.
edges.caveats: Most of the strongest data come from sport-related concussion in adolescents and young adults, so generalization to all concussion settings is imperfect. The intervention also requires some monitoring or testing to identify the symptom threshold; it is not simply unrestricted exercise.

evidence.citation: Leddy JJ et al 2019 JAMA Pediatr
evidence.notes: Early Subthreshold Aerobic Exercise for Sport-Related Concussion: A Randomized Clinical Trial.

evidence.citation: Hutchison MG et al 2022 PLoS One
